chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in a garment of dībāj, and he said: “So long as there are no images in it, there is no harm.”

The first point regarding this report is that we have already narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام that which conflicts with this report, and it is not permissible for his statements عليه السلام to differ.

Then, there is nothing in the outward sense of this report to indicate that there is no harm in praying in it under every circumstance. Since this is not apparent in its outward sense, we restrict it to the state of war rather than the state of choice; and that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.التَّمَاثِيلُ: images or figures depicted on the garment
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer under legal discussion
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith being examined
key_terms.ثَوْبِ دِيبَاجٍ: a garment of dībāj, referring to a silk or brocade cloth
key_terms.حَالِ الِاخْتِيَارِ: the condition of choice or normal non-compelled circumstance
key_terms.حَالِ الْحَرْبِ: the condition of war, a circumstance used to qualify the ruling
key_terms.ظَاهِرِ: the outward or apparent meaning of the text

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in a silk garment if it has no images?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) in a garment of dībāj, stating that there is no harm if it does not contain images. The accompanying discussion reconciles this narration with other reports from al-Riḍā عليه السلام by restricting its application to a condition such as war rather than normal voluntary circumstances.
